security_audit.summary: The skill is a genuine authorized-security Nmap guide, but it contains substantial dual-use reconnaissance content, elevated scan modes, evasion guidance, exploit/brute-force script workflows, and Metasploit integration. Many static findings in templates and references are false positives, but the main SKILL.md content and the CI curl-to-bash installer present real publication risks.

remediation.issue: Evasion and source-spoofing instructions in the main workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Remove or heavily gate fragmentation, decoy, spoofing, proxy, and idle-scan examples; keep only defensive detection guidance unless explicit marketplace policy allows them.

remediation.issue: Exploit, brute-force, intrusive, and DoS-related NSE categories are presented as usable scanning options.
remediation.suggestion: Limit default guidance to safe and default NSE scripts, and move intrusive checks behind explicit authorization, lab-only warnings, and safer validation alternatives.

remediation.issue: The CI template installs tfsec by piping a remote script directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash installation with a pinned release checksum, a trusted package manager, or a maintained GitHub Action with version pinning.

remediation.issue: Metasploit integration links reconnaissance output to exploitation tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Metasploit workflow references or restrict them to clearly separated, authorized lab documentation with strong legal and safety boundaries.

content.user_title: Map Networks with Authorized Nmap Workflows
content.value_statement: Network teams need repeatable reconnaissance steps that keep scope, timing, and reporting clear. This skill provides structured Nmap workflows for authorized asset discovery, service enumeration, and vulnerability validation.
actual_capabilities: Guides authorization, scope confirmation, scan windows, and emergency contact checks before scanning.
Provides Nmap host discovery workflows using ICMP, ARP, TCP, UDP, and no-ping techniques.
Shows port scanning options for common ports, full ranges, specific ports, timing, and rate limits.
Covers service version detection, OS fingerprinting, and service-specific enumeration examples.
Describes NSE script categories and vulnerability checks for common network services.
Explains output formats, report conversion, scan logging, and CI pipeline integration patterns.
limitations: The skill does not verify that the user has authorization for a target network.
Several workflows can be disruptive if used against production systems without controls.
It provides guidance only and does not execute scans, collect results, or validate findings automatically.
Some examples include intrusive or evasive scan modes that may be inappropriate for routine assessments.

use_cases.title: Validate an Internal Network Segment
use_cases.description: Plan a scoped Nmap scan that discovers live hosts, open ports, service versions, and segmentation gaps.

use_cases.title: Prepare an External Perimeter Review
use_cases.description: Build a phased reconnaissance workflow for approved external ranges with documented rate limits and outputs.

use_cases.title: Check Compliance Scan Evidence
use_cases.description: Translate scan goals into commands, logging requirements, and report artifacts for audit evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Authorized Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe Nmap plan for an authorized /24 network. Include scope checks, host discovery, port scanning, and output files.

prompt_templates.title: Enumerate Services for Live Hosts
prompt_templates.prompt: Given a list of approved live hosts, design an Nmap service enumeration workflow with version detection, useful scripts, and report outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a Low-Impact Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Adjust an Nmap assessment for a sensitive production network. Include timing, rate limits, maintenance windows, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Reconnaissance Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete authorized Nmap reconnaissance runbook for internal and external assets. Include evidence handling, false-positive review, and executive reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan discovery and port scanning for an approved internal subnet.
output_examples.output: A staged scan plan with authorization checks, live-host discovery, common-port scanning, service detection, rate limits, and named result files.

output_examples.input: Summarize how to report Nmap findings to a security team.
output_examples.output: A concise report outline covering scope, scan timing, discovered hosts, exposed services, suspected vulnerabilities, false-positive checks, and remediation owners.

output_examples.input: Tune Nmap scanning for a fragile production environment.
output_examples.output: A cautious workflow that uses approved windows, reduced timing, packet-rate limits, smaller target batches, monitoring contacts, and rollback instructions.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, exact scope, and maintenance windows before any scan activity.
Start with low-impact discovery and rate-limited scans before using intrusive scripts or full-port sweeps.
Keep scan logs, command history, source IP details, timestamps, and validation notes with each report.
anti_patterns: Scanning networks, hosts, or ports that are outside the approved scope.
Running exploit, brute-force, evasive, or denial-of-service scripts during routine discovery.
Treating NSE vulnerability output as final proof without manual validation and owner review.

faq.question: Does this skill run Nmap automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and command patterns that a user may apply in an authorized environment.

faq.question: Is authorization required before using these workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. Network scanning must be limited to systems where the user has explicit written permission.

faq.question: Can the examples disrupt services?
faq.answer: Yes. Full-port scans, UDP scans, vulnerability scripts, and aggressive timing can affect fragile services.

faq.question: Does the skill include reporting guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Nmap output formats, XML conversion, grepable output, audit logs, and report artifacts.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should intrusive NSE scripts be used by default?
faq.answer: No. Use safe scripts first and reserve intrusive checks for explicitly approved testing windows.
